reserve_musket.name: French reserve musket
reserve_musket.description: Worn depot arms. Cheap to field, with slower loading and less consistent fire.

charleville_1766.name: Charleville M1766
charleville_1766.description: Older service muskets retained in the depots. A useful step above worn reserve arms.

republican_musket.name: Republican composite musket
republican_musket.description: Mixed-pattern smoothbores assembled from serviceable parts. Inexpensive, but less uniform than regulation arms.

musket.name: Charleville M1777
musket.description: Regulation smoothbore musket and socket bayonet. Balanced issue for trained line infantry.

improved.name: M1777 arsenal-selected
improved.description: Inspected and carefully fitted M1777 arms, not a later model. Modest consistency gains at a higher replacement cost.

rifle.name: Versailles specialist rifle
rifle.description: Scarce specialist rifles. Accurate at distance, but slow to load and costly to replace. Demo availability is illustrative.

austrian_reserve.name: Austrian reserve musket
austrian_reserve.description: Older worn depot smoothbores. Low purchase cost offsets inconsistent fire and slower handling.

austrian_1784.name: Austrian M1784 musket
austrian_1784.description: Austrian regulation infantry musket and bayonet. Effective standard equipment, also usable when captured.

austrian_selected.name: M1784 arsenal-selected
austrian_selected.description: Inspected M1784 muskets selected for uniform service condition. A modest improvement rather than a new technology.

jager_rifle.name: Austrian Jager Stutzen
jager_rifle.description: Limited-issue rifled arms for trained marksmen. Strong aimed fire, long reload, and scarce reserve stocks.

sabre.name: Light cavalry sabre
sabre.description: Sabre equipment for cavalry fighting at close quarters. No long-arm firearm.

carbine.name: M1777 dragoon musket
carbine.description: Dragoon long arm with a retained cavalry sabre. Dismount for steadier fire; mounted volleys are less accurate.

hussar_carbine.name: M1786 hussar carbine
hussar_carbine.description: Short cavalry firearm carried alongside the sabre. Handy but out-ranged by infantry muskets.

austrian_carbine.name: Austrian cavalry carbine
austrian_carbine.description: Pre-1798 cavalry firearm and sabre equipment. Short-range fire complements, rather than replaces, shock action.

french_4pdr.name: Gribeauval 4-pounder
french_4pdr.description: Light field gun. Quick deployment and easy movement, trading reach and weight of shot for mobility.

cannon.name: Gribeauval 8-pounder
cannon.description: French medium field gun with round shot and close-range canister. Balanced power, reach, and handling.

french_12pdr.name: Gribeauval 12-pounder
french_12pdr.description: Heavy field gun. Powerful long-range fire, but slow movement, lengthy deployment, and high ammunition demand.

howitzer.name: French 6-inch howitzer
howitzer.description: Explosive shells on an arcing trajectory against spotted formations. Terrain clearance is checked; close targets receive canister.

austrian_3pdr.name: Austrian 3-pounder
austrian_3pdr.description: Light regimental gun. Cheap and mobile, but outmatched by heavier batteries at distance.

austrian_6pdr.name: Austrian 6-pounder
austrian_6pdr.description: Austrian medium field gun. A useful captured battery with a balance of mobility, round shot, and canister.

austrian_12pdr.name: Austrian 12-pounder
austrian_12pdr.description: Heavy Austrian battery equipment. Strong long-range fire at the cost of slower relocation and heavier supply consumption.

austrian_howitzer.name: Austrian 7-pounder howitzer
austrian_howitzer.description: Austrian explosive-shell howitzer. Arcing fire can clear low obstacles when the target is spotted and the trajectory is clear.
